title: Microsoft Taps AMD For At Scale AI CPU And GPU Clusters
gist: Ahead of AMD's Advancing AI 2026 event, Microsoft and AMD announced a large-scale Azure deployment built on AMD's 'Helios' rackscale design - MI455X GPUs, Venice Epyc 9006 CPUs, Pensando DPUs and ROCm - which The Next Platform estimates at hundreds of thousands of GPUs and $5 billion to $10 billion, specifically targeted at frontier-model inference. Timothy Prickett Morgan still puts Microsoft's Nvidia-to-AMD GPU split at roughly 70/30 or 75/25 and argues accelerator share is set almost entirely by HBM memory allocation.

insights.claim: The double-wide AMD Helios rack packs 4,600 Zen 6 CPU cores across 18 compute trays holding one CPU and four GPUs each, working out to 256 cores per Venice processor and 72 GPUs per rack.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Concrete rack density to compare against Nvidia rackscale designs when modeling per-rack revenue and power draw.
insights.quote: The double-wide Helios rack has 4,600 Zen 6 CPU cores across 18 compute trays with one CPU and four GPUs each.

insights.claim: A single Helios rack delivers 2.9 exaflops at FP4 precision across 18,000 GPU compute units, with 31 TB of HBM4 stacked memory and 43 TB/sec of aggregate bandwidth routed through Pensando DPUs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The HBM capacity per rack is the binding constraint on how many of these AMD can actually ship.
insights.locator: it also works out to 18,000 GPU compute units

insights.claim: The Pensando DPUs in the Helios rack are programmable in the P4 language, a feature Microsoft specifically valued given it has been perhaps the dominant deployer of Pensando DPUs to date.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Explains why Microsoft in particular anchors the AMD rackscale win - an existing DPU install base creates switching costs in AMD's favor.
insights.quote: This is a key feature, and one that Microsoft took a shining to as it has been perhaps the dominant deployer of Pensando DPUs to date.
insights.locator: which are programmable on the P4 language

insights.claim: Neither Microsoft nor AMD disclosed the deal value, but The Next Platform expects the Helios rack purchase to cover hundreds of thousands of GPUs and be worth between $5 billion and $10 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A concrete, if estimated, revenue anchor for AMD's 2026-2027 datacenter GPU line from a single customer.
insights.quote: we expect it to be for hundreds of thousands of GPUs and between $5 billion and $10 billion.
insights.locator: Neither Microsoft nor AMD are talking about how much money

insights.claim: The Microsoft Helios deployment is very specifically targeted at running inference for frontier models on the Azure cloud rather than training, confirming AMD's positioning as an inference-first challenger.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Validates the inference mix-shift thesis with an actual hyperscaler purchase, not a forecast.
insights.quote: it is very specifically targeted at running inference for frontier models on the Azure cloud.
insights.locator: What we do know for sure is that this is a very large scale deployment

insights.claim: Microsoft has additionally committed to all-CPU Venice Epyc clusters behind two new Azure instance families: HDv2 aimed at agentic AI workloads and their data pipeline processing, and HXv2 with presumably more cores aimed at electronic design automation for chips.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: First concrete cloud SKU evidence that the agentic AI CPU category is being productized, not just forecast.
insights.locator: Microsoft has committed to rolling out clusters of Venice Epyc CPUs

insights.claim: Microsoft is porting its Azure Boost networking and storage virtualization from the homegrown DPU it deployed in November 2024 to P4 routines on AMD Pensando DPUs, ceding part of its custom silicon stack back to a merchant vendor.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A rare reversal of the hyperscaler in-house silicon trend and a direct revenue transfer to AMD's networking franchise.
insights.locator: Microsoft is working with AMD to move its Azure Boost acceleration software

insights.claim: The author estimates Microsoft's GPU acquisitions are split roughly 70/30 or 75/25 in Nvidia's favor over AMD, so the headline Helios win does not change the underlying market structure.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Caps how much of a share-shift narrative to read into the announcement; AMD is gaining at the margin, not displacing.
insights.locator: we still believe that the distribution of GPU acquisitions

insights.claim: AI accelerator market share is fundamentally determined by HBM memory allocation - if Nvidia has 80 percent of the HBM it sells roughly 80 percent of the XPUs - making memory supply contracts the real competitive battleground.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Reduces the accelerator share question to a single observable: HBM supply agreements with the memory makers.
insights.quote: It is all about who gets what allocations of HBM memory, and when. If Nvidia has 80 percent of the HBM, it sells 80 percent of the XPUs, more or less. It really is that simple.
insights.locator: It is all about who gets what allocations of HBM memory

insights.claim: If AMD's share of the AI training and inference pie is growing then its HBM allocations must also be growing, and the author warns that otherwise there are going to be massive lawsuits about antitrust and restraint of trade.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Flags HBM allocation practices as a live legal risk channel that could force supply reallocation independent of demand.
insights.quote: They better be, or there are going to be some massive lawsuits about antitrust and restraint of trade.
insights.locator: But we do think that AMD's share of the AI training and inference pie

insights.claim: Both Microsoft and Meta Platforms are enthusiastic supporters of the ESUN coherent memory fabric protocol emerging as an alternative to Nvidia's NVLink/NVSwitch combo and to the UALink protocol AMD and partners launched in May 2024.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The scale-up fabric standard determines which switch silicon vendors capture the fastest-growing networking layer, and it is not yet settled.
insights.locator: Both Microsoft and Meta Platforms are enthusiastic supporters

insights.claim: Microsoft may start with ESUN running on low latency Ethernet switches in its initial Helios racks and move to UALink switches later, though the author concedes this remains unclear until Microsoft chooses to disclose it.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Watch the initial Helios scale-up choice as the leading signal for whether UALink becomes a real standard or stays a spec.
insights.locator: Microsoft may be starting with ESUN running on low latency Ethernet switches

insights.claim: The scale-out network for the Helios racks is almost certainly Ethernet and Arista Networks is the likely switch supplier, per the author's inference rather than any announcement.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A speculative but specific read-through to Arista's AI-datacenter order book.
insights.quote: The scale out networking for the Helios racks is no doubt Ethernet, and it is very likely that Arista Networks is the supplier of the switches for this part of the network.
insights.locator: The scale out networking for the Helios racks

insights.claim: Every GPU and CPU that AMD and Nvidia can make for the rest of 2026 has already been sold even though not all of it has been manufactured, meaning product launches now serve marketing rather than demand generation.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: In a sold-out market, announcements are share-of-mind, not order flow; supply and HBM allocation are the only variables that move revenue.
insights.quote: Every GPU and every CPU that AMD and Nvidia can make for the rest of 2026 has already been long since sold even if they have not all been manufactured as yet.
insights.locator: We live in a weird time

insights.claim: AMD is just about the only company applying direct pressure on Nvidia in both GPU-accelerated systems and all-CPU clusters, the two areas where Nvidia is generating its largest profits.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Positions AMD as the sole credible second source, which is what makes hyperscaler dual-sourcing announcements structurally valuable to it.
insights.locator: AMD is just about the only company applying direct pressure
